item.title: ‘Never Speak About It’: Leaked Audit Reveals the UN’s Palantir Problem
item.description: The World Food Programme (WFP) manages one of the biggest biometric databases in the world. Its SCOPE system contains information on millions of people, many of them beneficiaries of global humanitarian aid. To help the WFP track humanitarian aid and manage its supply-chain data, Palantir developed the Digital Operations and Transformation System (DOTS). Founded in 2003, Palantir — ... Read more

item.title: In Taliban-Ruled Afghanistan, One Woman Refuses a Life of Dependence
item.description: The author is an Afghanistan-based female journalist, trained with Finnish support before the Taliban take-over. Her identity is withheld for security reasons

item.title: Food prices edged up in July amid heatwaves and energy price hikes
item.description: The cost of key foods edged up last month as searing heatwaves and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty impacted energy prices around the world.

item.title: Ebola in DR Congo: Childhood deaths rise; hopes raised over new vaccine
item.description: More than 300 children have died in the Ebola outbreak in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), the UN said on Friday, as health experts urged trials of the only vaccine against the disease to halt further spread of the rare Bundibugyo species.

item.title: Peacock party takes pride of place in nod to decades of turbulent history
item.description: In a new twist on panda diplomacy, UN Geneva welcomed five young peacocks to the Palace of Nations on Friday, a gift of India that preserves a tradition of keeping the stately birds in the grounds, that predates both the global body and its ill-fated predecessor, the League of Nations.

item.title: Hiroshima’s Question: Will We Continue to Live Under the Nuclear Shadow?
item.description: On the 81st anniversary of the atomic bombing, Hiroshima’s Peace Declaration and the U.N. secretary-general’s message set out two possible futures as the global nuclear order frays
